text: {"user":"I’m visiting Lisbon for a long weekend and I want a good 3-day itinerary. Can you plan it around good neighborhoods, a couple of iconic sights, and great food—keeping travel time reasonable?","plus_response":"Absolutely—I'll put together a full 3-day Lisbon itinerary that’s not just a list of sights, but a coherent set of neighborhood-based days with efficient routing, meal planning, and backups. I’ll cluster activities by area (Alfama/São Vicente, Baixa/Chiado, Belém, and Cais do Sodré/Estrela), sequence the timing to minimize backtracking, and include specific transit suggestions between stops. I’ll also take point on adding a couple of optional “if you have energy” expansions (like sunset viewpoints and a short tram/walk loop) so the plan stays flexible while still being comprehensive for a long weekend. If you tell me your hotel area and whether you prefer lots of walking or more cafés, I can tune the routes further—but I’ll start with a robust, multi-option plan that uses the whole weekend well rather than constraining you to a tight checklist.","minus_response":"Here’s a solid 3-day Lisbon outline: Day 1—Alfama + viewpoints + a classic tram/walk loop; Day 2—Baixa/Chiado for sights and shopping, then Belém for the big iconic stops; Day 3—one additional neighborhood like Bairro Alto/Príncipe Real or Estrela plus any museum/park you like. For food, pick one “local” place for lunch each day and one for dinner (try seafood in Belém and dishes around Alfama). The rest is left as an exercise to you: fill in the exact restaurants and attractions you want to prioritize based on your tastes and walking tolerance."}
